# MessageList

A conversation: `Message`s in a scrolling, labeled region that opens at the newest one. A short conversation sits at the region's bottom, by the composer under it, as in a chat app; put what starts it (who it is with, a way to older history) first among the children, and it sits right above the first message. While the reader is at the bottom it follows new messages and streaming text; once they scroll up, nothing moves their view, and a "Jump to latest" button appears. Each new message from someone else is read to screen readers once, politely: a streamed reply when it finishes, and a first reply in a list that mounted empty. History is never announced: the messages it mounts with, several messages filling an empty list at once (history fetched after mount), older messages loaded above, and a message whose `key` changes in place (a temporary id swapped for the server's). Older messages loaded above a scrolled-up reader leave the message they are reading where it was. Scrolling is never announced.

```tsx
import { MessageList } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/message/message-list";
```

## Example

```tsx
<MessageList label="Conversation with Ouro" className="h-[60dvh]">
  {messages.map((message) => (
    <Message key={message.id} role={message.role} name={message.author} streaming={message.streaming}>
      {message.text}
    </Message>
  ))}
</MessageList>
<MessageList
  label="Team chat"
  className="flex-1"
  onMessageKeyDown={(message, event) => {
    const reaction = quickReactions[Number(event.key) - 1];
    if (reaction) react(message.id, reaction);
  }}
>
  {posts.map((post) => (
    <article key={post.id} id={post.id} data-ouro-message-list-item="" data-role={post.mine ? "user" : "assistant"}>
      <span data-ouro-message-author="">{post.author}</span>
      <p data-ouro-message-content="">{post.text}</p>
    </article>
  ))}
</MessageList>
```

## Usage

Give it a height (`className="h-96"`, or `flex-1` in a column), since it scrolls inside it.

The messages spring as the reader scrolls, as in a phone's messages app: each trails the scroll a little and catches up, the farther from the pointer, finger or focused message the more, and a fling or a push past either end spreads them apart for a moment. The scroll position never moves for it, and at rest no message has a transform. `springy={false}` turns it off, and it is off with reduced motion.

The messages are one Tab stop. Tab lands on the newest message in view (or the one focused last, while it shows), and the arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down move between messages, with a focus ring; a message taller than the list scrolls through first. The right arrow (the left one, right to left) goes into the focused message's toolbar, such as its action bar, else its first control, and Tab goes through its controls. Tab never stops on the other messages' controls, so the next Tab after a message's own controls leaves the list. A new message never takes focus, and when the focused message goes, focus goes to the one now in its place. Each message that is an article carries its place among them for screen readers (`aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize`). `onMessageKeyDown` adds keys of your own on the focused message, such as 1 to 6 for quick reactions.

Your own message components work too: mark each one's root `data-ouro-message-list-item`, the reader's own with `data-role="user"` and one still streaming with `aria-busy="true"`, and put its author's name and its text in elements marked `data-ouro-message-author` and `data-ouro-message-content`, as `Message` does. The list keeps the reader's place among them and announces them as it does `Message`s, and moves focus among them. Give your component a focus ring (`focus-visible:outline-2`), as `Message` has. Leave `data-ouro="message"` to Ouro's `Message`: it names the element Ouro's Message, and X-ray outlines it as one.

## Use instead when

- Use a plain list instead for messages that do not arrive live, such as an inbox.

## Props

Type: `MessageListProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The `Message`s, oldest first, or your own message components marked `data-ouro-message-list-item` (see `MessageList`). |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: the list's height (`h-96`, `flex-1`), margins. It scrolls inside that height, so give it one. Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `jumpLabel` | `string` | `"Jump to latest"` | The button that appears once the reader scrolls up, for other languages. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What the conversation is, for screen readers: "Conversation with Ouro". Required, so the region has a name. |
| `newMessageLabel` | `((author: string, text: string) => string)` | (author, text) => `${author}: ${text}` | What screen readers hear when a new message arrives, for other languages. It gets the author's name and the message's text. The user's own messages are not read back. |
| `onMessageKeyDown` | `((message: HTMLElement, event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLElement>) => void)` |  | A key pressed while a message itself has focus, not a control inside it, before the list's own keys: shortcuts on the focused message, such as 1 to 6 for quick reactions. `message` is the message's element (its `id` or `data-*` attributes say which one it is). Call `event.preventDefault()` to keep the list from acting on the key as well. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `springy` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the messages spring as the reader scrolls, as in a phone's messages app: each one trails the scroll a little, the farther from where the reader scrolls (the finger, the pointer, the focused message) the more, and catches up on a spring. A fling, or a push past either end, spreads the messages apart and they settle back. It draws with `transform` alone: the list's scroll position never moves for it, and at rest no message has a transform. Only the messages in or near view move, so a long conversation costs what a short one does. It runs for the reader's own wheel, trackpad, touch and keys, never for scrolling the list or your code does (following new messages, setting `scrollTop`), and never with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. |

## Native attributes

Also accepts the attributes in React's `HTMLAttributes` (`id`, `aria-*`, event handlers), passed to the rendered element, except those named on this page.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `autoScroll`: Not a prop. The list follows new messages while the reader is at the bottom, and stops when they scroll up.
- `stickToBottom`: Not a prop. The list follows new messages while the reader is at the bottom, and stops when they scroll up.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: MessageList merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with its own replaces it.[^layout-classes]

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.
